title: Sony BRAVIA XBR-55X850C (2015, SVP-DTV15 "BRAVIA 4K 2015" platform, MediaTek), US firmware
header:
Sony BRAVIA XBR-55X850C (2015, SVP-DTV15 "BRAVIA 4K 2015" platform, MediaTek), US firmware
Android TV 8.0 (API 26), build SVP4KDTV15_UC-user 8.0.0 OPR2.170623.027.S16 6.827, 1.5 GB RAM

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/sony-xbr-55x850c/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/sony-xbr-55x850c/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Same build as examples/sony-kd-65x9300d. Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (restore.sh's
default). The only other HOME handler is com.android.tv.settings. setupwraith has no HOME activity,
and the saved Wi-Fi belongs to android.uid.system, so it is left alone.
Live TV / input app: com.sony.dtv.tvx. Keep it: it also plays every HDMI input.
Keep: com.sony.dtv.tvinput.*, tvplayer*, braviasync* (HDMI-CEC), remotepairing, remotecontrolsettings,
uinputservice, imeproxy, settingsprovider, netflixmanager (Netflix button), duid.generator,
enclave.service, systemupdate, timers, all com.mediatek.* and mtktvapi.agent.
Left alone on purpose: the rest of com.sony.dtv.b2b.* (hotel/pro mode plumbing), webapi.core and
remoteaccess (Sony IP control), privacypolicy, sonyselect.overlay (a /vendor/overlay RRO),
DLNA (huey.dlna.*, sonyericsson.dlna*) and the USB media players (osat.*).
Nothing was disabled at the factory.

Notes from this firmware:
- Disabling tvlaunchercustomizer removes the notifications, Inputs and Timer icons from the stock
home's top bar; the remote's Input button still works through com.sony.dtv.tvx.
- build-and-install.sh hands Home over cleanly. Inputs lists HDMI 1-4 (with CEC names), Video 1/2
and Live TV; HDMI 1 opens in com.sony.dtv.tvx. Hide com.sony.dtv.tvx and set live_tv_package to it.
- Home, Input, Netflix, Back and Action Menu all work on the real remote with no key services.
- Used RAM went from 1,119 MB to 1,003 MB after this list, the launcher and a reboot. Boots straight
into the new launcher. com.sony.dtv.systembootmonitor crashes once at boot (Android 8 background
service limit); it is not in this list.
